messages.subject: screwed up OR inside the condition argument in the conditionPanel
parts:
i am trying to write a condition argument in the conditionalPanel based on the selection of the tab in the tabset panel.

conditionalPanel(
              condition = "input.tab == 'Fixed Warning Analysis' " || "input.tab == 'Warning Analysis'",
      selectInput(inputId="filter",label="Select Filter",choices=c("Business-Unit"="bu","Country"="country","Division"="division"),selected=NULL,multiple=FALSE)
    )

Error : 

Error in "input.tab == 'Fixed Warning Analysis'" | "input.tab == 'Warning Analysis'" : 
  operations are possible only for numeric, logical or complex types

i think the problem is in the comparison of the OR statement. can somebody correct me where i am doing the mistake. I belief it is very simple enough.

Regards
Koushik Saha

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Re: screwed up OR inside the condition argument in the conditionPanel
parts:
If you'd included a minimal example, together with ui.R and server.R, I could have played around to experiment. I'm not an expert, but I just recently asked a question about conditionalPanel conditions and am quite curious about this too. 

If I'm not mistaken, in

conditionalPanel(condition = "blabla", etc.)

the blabla should be written in javascript, not in R. So my impression is that if you write "bla" || "bla" you are breaking the condition in two separate parts. I think you need to have both clauses and the javascript equivalent of || inside "".  I'm not sure you see, but until someone more knowledgeable chimes in, you can perhaps look in that direction.

How about writing your condition in R on the server side and passing it to the conditionalPanel via an output$Condition? 

Not sure if that would work, something like this maybe:

# ui.R

conditionalPanel(condition = "output.Condition == true'", etc.

# server.R

output$Condition <- renderText({
  if " input$tab == 'Fixed Warning Analysis' || input$tab == 'Warning Analysis' "
 return(1) # or maybe return("true") or return(TRUE) or return(print("1")) or something to that effect
})
